McLaren.summary: McLaren’s new front wing now features re‑shaped endplates that smooth the air coming off the nose, giving the car a cleaner‑swept front end. The tweak should boost grip on the corners and keep the car more stable through high‑speed sections, helping the drivers extract a few extra tenths on the lap. In short, it’s a subtle aero fix that could translate into better cornering speed and a stronger overall race pace.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has added tiny winglets right along the centre of the rear wing. These little pieces fine‑tune the aerodynamics, giving the car a bit more rear‑end stability when it’s pushing hard through corners. The result should be a smoother, more predictable handling package for this weekend’s track.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has reshaped the sections where the front‑wing panels meet the endplates, tweaking the shape to smooth out airflow and give the car a more stable front end. They’ve also added a bit more camber (tilt) to the wing flaps, widening the car’s handling window so drivers can dial in the perfect balance more easily. Together, these tweaks should improve corner grip and give the team a little extra flexibility in setting up the car for this weekend’s track.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has reshaped the front wing and nose, adding new vanes and a dive‑plane that smooth out the airflow and give the car a more stable front end. The floor, diffuser and rear‑corner winglets have been slimmed and re‑profiled to generate extra down‑force without a big drag penalty, while the side‑pod shoulder has been puffed up to tidy up the air that reaches the rear. In short, the car should feel stickier and more balanced this weekend, giving the drivers better grip into corners and a stronger push on the straights.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has added new little winglets and a modest extension to the rear wing’s third element, giving the car a boost in rear‑end grip. The tweak tightens the car’s balance in fast corners and helps keep it stable under heavy braking, which should translate into better lap times and more confidence for the drivers this weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has tweaked the front wing to give the car a wider range of balance settings and added extra flap‑gurney options, letting the team fine‑tune how much front‑end grip they need for the particular track layout. They’ve also reshaped the rear diffuser and merged it more tightly with the crash structure, which smooths the airflow off the back and boosts overall down‑force. Together these changes should make the car more adaptable and quicker through the corners and on the straights for this weekend’s race.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has tweaked the rear impact structure, tightening it up to better handle the forces hitting the back of the car. The change sharpens rear‑end stability and gives the chassis a more predictable feel under braking and corner exit. In short, it should help the drivers keep the car glued to the track and extract a few extra tenths over the weekend.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has added a set of cooling louvres to the upper part of the rear sidepod, letting heat escape more efficiently so the power unit can stay in its sweet spot longer. They’ve also fitted a sleek fairing around the rear‑wing SLM actuator, trimming unwanted drag and giving the car a cleaner airflow. Together these tweaks mean the car runs cooler and faster on the straights, giving drivers a tangible edge right out of the gate this weekend.
